title: American Studies, B.A. (University College)
notes: BRANDYWINE (Pattern B, new plan file — added for the University College branch-campus pass). American Studies has no University Park major of this name at all (checked: the closest UP names, African American Studies (AFAM) and African and African American Studies, are a genuinely different program about a different subject, not this one) — the bulletin's own American Studies, B.A. only exists as a University College page, whose real 'Where can I complete this program?' section reads 'Begin Campus: Any Penn State Campus' / 'End Campus: Brandywine' (Abington and Capital/Harrisburg have their own separate American Studies, B.A. pages, not modeled here). American Studies is one of Brandywine's 14 real on-site-completable bachelor's degrees (brandywine.psu.edu). Built directly from the University College bulletin's own 'American Studies, B.A. at Brandywine Campus' Suggested Academic Plan PDF (american-studies-ba_suggestedacademicplantext.pdf, 2026-27 edition) — every course and credit value below is taken verbatim from that Brandywine-specific table, not the generic Abington/Harrisburg variants also on the same page family. Real major requirements (from the same page): AMST 100 (Intro to American Studies, C-required) + AMST 491W taken twice with different topics as the department's own repeatable capstone (6cr total, C-required, also satisfies University Writing Across the Curriculum) + 24cr of 'Supporting Courses' cross-listed across American literature, history, art/philosophy/religion, and social sciences (9cr in each of two areas, 6cr in one additional area, at least 12cr at the 400 level) = 33cr major total. The department does not publish an enumerable area-to-course list for that 24cr Supporting Courses requirement (it is adviser-driven, cutting across AMST/ENGL/HIST/PHIL/ARTH/HDFS/PLSC and more) — modeled as generic 'American Focused Course' slots at the levels the real Brandywine plan itself specifies (1-199, 1-299, 400), the same convention used for ENGL's own unenumerable 'Concentration Course' era-group slots. The two AMST 491W capstone occurrences are modeled as two separate generic 'slot' items (not 'course' items) each carrying a 'match': '^AMST 491W$' regex for real-transcript recognition, rather than two literal course items sharing the identical single option ['AMST 491W'] — tried the literal-course-item approach first (the same repeatable-course pattern that already works for MUSED's MUSIC 153/154 pair) and found it does NOT generalize to a truly single-option repeat: MUSED's pair works because it offers two DIFFERENT real codes (153 or 154) so each item claims a different course, but a single ['AMST 491W'] option repeated twice hits a genuine engine limitation — plan_progress's one-completed-code-per-item matching lets only the first (earlier) item ever claim 'AMST 491W' once it's in the student's completed set, so build_full_plan's simulator kept re-recommending the second item's identical course forever (24 simulated terms, never converging) since the code was never allowed to satisfy the second slot. Modeling both as generic slots (same convention already used for TURF 495 and ARCH 491's second enrollment) sidesteps this entirely while still crediting the real 6cr total and still recognizing a real completed AMST 491W against either slot via match. The 400-level 'American Focused Course' slots (including the two 'or Major Related Internship' variants, where the internship alternative has no fixed course code) are additionally wired with a real 'match' regex against every actual AMST 4xx course this session scraped fresh into catalogs/amst_catalog.json (bulletins.psu.edu/university-course-descriptions/undergraduate/amst/), so a student's real completed 400-level AMST course (e.g. AMST 412, AMST 441, AMST 480) is recognized against these slots — the plan does not require the match to be an exact fit, matching the CASBA/ENGL 400-level convention. World Language levels 1-3 and the B.A. Fields/World Cultures requirements are modeled as generic credit slots (no fixed PSU code — the real requirement varies by which language and which adviser-approved field a student picks), the same convention used across every other B.A. already in this repo (ENGL, CASBA, HIST). Gen Ed slots are left generic except the two explicit '(GHW)' 1.5-credit half-slots the real Brandywine suggested plan itself calls out. Chose the low end of each credit range shown on the bulletin (World Language 4cr/level, not 4-6; World-Language-or-Gen-Ed slot at 4cr) to land on a clean, schedulable 120-credit total, within the bulletin's own stated 119-124cr range. 'etm' marks AMST 100 and the first-year writing course as the courses the rest of the sequence assumes are done, though this department has no real enforced prereq chain (confirmed: every AMST course this session scraped came back with an empty prereq_groups list).
